title: Wheel and Tire Safety Decisions
introduction:
I check wheel and tire safety at several stages: before inflation, before removing a damaged wheel, when matching parts and after installation. Holding air is only part of the picture; compatibility, structural condition and wheel-nut retention matter too.

These warnings establish handling rules and prohibited repairs. They are not a complete tire-mounting or wheel-installation procedure and do not specify inflation pressures or wheel-nut torque. The additional retightening instruction expressly applies only to the stated rear-wheel configuration.

edits.text: WARNING: If a tire has been run flat, remove it from the wheel and inspect it for damage before attempting inflation. Never inflate it without that inspection. A damaged tire can fail during inflation and cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: The required inspection comes before adding air and requires removing the tire from the wheel, not merely taking the wheel off the vehicle.

edits.text: WARNING: Never mount tube-type tires on tubeless wheels or tubeless tires on tube-type wheels. Either incorrect combination can allow the tire to separate from the wheel and may seriously injure vehicle occupants.
edits.why: Tire and wheel construction types must be compatible as well as correctly sized.

edits.text: WARNING: Deflate the tire on a cracked wheel before removing that wheel from the vehicle. Cracked wheels are dangerous; failing to deflate the tire first may cause serious personal injury.
edits.why: The sequence matters: deflation must precede removal of the wheel from the vehicle.

edits.text: WARNING: After reinstalling a wheel, retighten its wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi). For dual rear wheel (DRW) vehicles only, retighten them again within 800 km (500 mi). Wheels can loosen after their initial tightening; failing to perform the required retightening may seriously injure vehicle occupants.
edits.why: Retightening is a required follow-up to installation. The additional interval is conditional on the specified wheel configuration.

edits.text: WARNING: Always match tire size to wheel size during assembly. A mismatch can damage the tire bead or allow the tire to separate from the wheel, potentially causing serious personal injury to the technician or vehicle occupants.
edits.why: Size compatibility is a separate check from matching tube-type and tubeless construction.

edits.text: WARNING: Never weld or peen a wheel. If a wheel needs either type of repair, install a new wheel instead. Disregarding these instructions can lead to wheel failure and serious personal injury.
edits.why: This is a replacement requirement, not permission to restore the wheel by either prohibited method.
